newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian steel mill tender extended until Sept 30.
newsitem.headline: Croatian steel mill tender extended until Sept 30.

text.p: An international tender for a majority stake in Croatian steel mill Zeljezara Sisak has been extended until September 30, a government official said on Monday.
A number of potential buyers bought project documentation for Metaval, Zeljezara's core business subsidiary which was advertised for sale in July, Assistant Economy Minister Ivana Halle told Reuters.
She declined to say whether any definite bids yet had been received yet.
Croatian government, as a majority owner of the heavily indebted holding company, had set no target price in the tender.
It was seeking "strategic partners" to strengthen Metaval's international and domestic position, probably through hefty investment in the existing production lines.

The company said in July Swiss, Austrian and Italian firms were interested. Metaval is the country's main producer of steel and steel semi-products, strip, billets, seamless and welded hot- and cold-rolled tubes and pipes.
But industry analysts estimate between 30 and 40 million German marks would be needed to raise productivity and remove bottlenecks.
They also say the company would have to be trimmed down in size to some 2,500 instead of the current 3,100 workers.
All of Zeljezara holding was valued at roughly 240 million marks four years ago. Its debts are thought to have mounted to as much as 170 million, dampening its attractiveness.
However, the core business was put up for sale clear of all debts, taken over by government as a first step in Zeljezara's much delayed restructuring.

In exchange its creditors, including Privredna Banka Zagreb which is itself due for a radical overhaul, are to get equity stakes in the remaining, healthy parts of the holding. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-4557075
